title: NBA Offseason Daily Digest
subtitle: July 25, 2026 - Free Agency & Trade Frenzy Continues!

items.headline: LeBron James Joins Philadelphia 76ers on Two-Year Deal
items.summary: In a seismic shift in the NBA landscape, four-time MVP LeBron James has officially signed a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers. James, 41, announced his decision to join the Sixers, seeking another championship alongside Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, and Joel Embiid. The move culminates weeks of speculation following his departure from the Lakers, with Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro even proclaiming July 24, 2026, as 'LeBron James Day' in celebration.

items.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo Traded to Miami Heat in Blockbuster Deal
items.summary: Two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo is heading to South Beach as the Milwaukee Bucks traded the superstar forward to the Miami Heat. In return, Milwaukee acquired Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakučionis, the No. 13 pick in the 2026 draft, first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, a 2030 pick swap, and a 2033 second-round pick. This monumental trade marks one of the most significant moves in a wild NBA offseason.

items.headline: Hawks Acquire Lu Dort in Three-Team Trade
items.summary: The Atlanta Hawks have bolstered their backcourt, acquiring guard Luguentz Dort and guard Ryan Nembhard in a three-team deal involving the OKC Thunder and Dallas Mavericks. The Mavericks received forward Zaccharie Risacher, while the Thunder landed three future second-round picks.

items.headline: Celtics Trade Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia 76ers
items.summary: Weeks of speculation have ended with the Boston Celtics trading All-NBA forward Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers. This move comes as the 76ers make significant roster enhancements, including the recent signing of LeBron James.

items.headline: Pistons Send Caris LeVert to Milwaukee Bucks
items.summary: The Detroit Pistons have traded guard Caris LeVert to the Milwaukee Bucks, also sending two second-round picks along with him. This deal provides the Bucks with additional guard depth.

items.headline: Lakers Trade Deandre Ayton to Washington Wizards
items.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are continuing their frontcourt reshuffle post-LeBron, sending center Deandre Ayton to the Washington Wizards. This move helps the Lakers create cap space and flexibility.

items.headline: Julius Randle Heads to Brooklyn Nets in Three-Team Trade
items.summary: In another complex three-team deal, the Minnesota Timberwolves are trading forward Julius Randle to the Brooklyn Nets. The Nets also acquire the No. 28 pick in the 2026 draft, while the Chicago Bulls receive center Nic Claxton, and Minnesota lands forward Mo Gueye and the No. 33 pick.

items.headline: Warriors and Heat Pursue DeMar DeRozan
items.summary: Following LeBron James' decision, the Miami Heat and Golden State Warriors are reportedly turning their attention to six-time NBA All-Star free agent DeMar DeRozan. Both teams have been in contact with DeRozan, who could provide a significant veteran presence.

items.headline: Lakers Maintain Contact with Jonathan Kuminga's Representatives
items.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers remain active in the free-agent market, with president of basketball operations Rob Pelinka reportedly continuing to contact Jonathan Kuminga's representatives despite the two sides not yet reaching an agreement. The Lakers are looking to finalize their roster for the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: 2026 NBA Summer League Concludes with Record Attendance
items.summary: The 2026 NBA Summer League in Las Vegas officially wrapped up on July 19, concluding a successful run from July 9. The event set an attendance record with over 156,000 attendees, and ESPN viewership was up 61%, highlighting the significant interest in the league's newest talent.

items.headline: Rookie Standouts Shine at Summer League
items.summary: The 2026 rookie class lived up to its tremendous hype at the Summer League. No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa (Wizards) showed his high ceiling, while No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson showcased excellent shot creation. Cameron Boozer, the third overall pick, led his team to the Summer League Final with his smart and mature offensive game. Caleb Wilson (Bulls), drafted fourth, saw his stock rise significantly after a scintillating 35-point debut.

items.headline: Offseason Coaching Carousel Continues
items.summary: The coaching landscape has seen several changes this offseason. Doc Rivers resigned as head coach of the Milwaukee Bucks on April 13, followed by Billy Donovan stepping down from the Chicago Bulls on April 21. The Bucks then hired Taylor Jenkins on April 30. Jamahl Mosley was fired by the Orlando Magic on May 4 but quickly hired by the New Orleans Pelicans on May 18. Additionally, Jason Kidd and the Dallas Mavericks mutually agreed to part ways on May 19.
